newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech to review FCC order, may refile.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech to review FCC order, may refile.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Tuesday it will review an order issued by the Federal Communications Commission rejecting its bid to enter the long-distance telephone business and may refile its request.
"Going forward, we will take whatever steps are necessary to resolve this issue properly," Richard Notebaert, Ameritech chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

"We will study the order when it's issued, we will work vigorously to fulfill any remaining requirements, and then we'll refile to offer long distance -- in Michigan as well as the other four states we serve," he said.

The FCC earlier Tuesday rejected Ameritech's bid to become the first major communications company approved to provide long distance service within its local service territory under the terms of the 1996 federal Telecommunications Act.
But in a partial victory for Ameritech, the FCC provided a detailed roadmap for how the Chicago-based carrier and other regional Bells can enter the $80 billion long-distance business.

"If the FCC's order includes hurdles that are impossible for any company to meet, or if it leaves the door open to constantly adding new hurdles beyond what's in the order, or if it includes a Catch-22 -- such as the metrics test that Congress specifically rejected -- then that roadmap is not feasible," Notebaert said. "That would be a real letdown to customers and a disservice to the industry, because a realistic roadmap is exactly what we need to make competition work for customers."
Ameritech provides local and long distance telephone, cellular, paging, security monitoring, cable TV, electronic commerce and on-line services.
